mutation_targets.rationale: Removing F_CareTeamGating lets the model find a world where a clinician with no care-team membership obtains a Permitted outcome on RecordLookup or AddNote, directly violating FR-004.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_CareTeamGatingViolation { some op: Operation | op.opKind = RecordLookup and op.opOutcome = Permitted and op.opCaller.userRole = Doctor and (no m: CareTeamMembership | m.ctmMember = op.opCaller and m.ctmPatient = op.opPatient) }

mutation_targets.rationale: Removing F_AuditCorrespondence allows the model to produce an Operation with an audit entry whose accessor differs from the operation's caller, and allows orphan audit entries, violating both always-on audit and attribution correctness.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_AuditCorrespondenceViolation { some op: Operation | op.opAudit.auditAccessor != op.opCaller }

mutation_targets.rationale: Removing F_PermissionMatrix lets PermMatrix.Allowed become arbitrary, making it possible for HospitalAdministrator to have RecordLookup in the allowed set, breaking LeastPrivilege and PermissionCompleteness.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_PermissionMatrixViolation { HospitalAdministrator -> RecordLookup in PermMatrix.Allowed }

mutation_targets.rationale: Removing F_AppendOnlyClinicalNotes allows two distinct Permitted AddNote operations to link to the same ClinicalNote atom, simulating a 'reuse/overwrite' of a note entry that violates the append-only invariant.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_AppendOnlyViolation { some disj op1, op2: Operation | op1.opKind = AddNote and op1.opOutcome = Permitted and op2.opKind = AddNote and op2.opOutcome = Permitted and op1.opAudit.auditLinkedNote = op2.opAudit.auditLinkedNote }

mutation_targets.rationale: Removing F_ClinicalEndpointsBlockAdmin allows a model world where a HospitalAdministrator caller obtains Permitted on AddNote, directly violating FR-005 administrator content-blindness.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_AdminContentViolation { some op: Operation | op.opCaller.userRole = HospitalAdministrator and op.opKind = AddNote and op.opOutcome = Permitted }

mutation_targets.rationale: Removing F_PermittedResponseIsSuccess allows the model to assign SuccessResponse to a Denied outcome, meaning both denied and permitted operations produce the same SuccessResponse — or inversely, Denied produces a distinct response shape that leaks existence of the resource.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_LeakageViolation { some op: Operation | op.opOutcome = Denied and op.opResponse = SuccessResponse }
